title: How an erection actually happens
body:
An erection is mostly a blood flow event, triggered by a mix of physical and mental signals. Arousal — from touch, thought, or both — sends a signal that relaxes smooth muscle in two chambers of the penis (the corpora cavernosa). That relaxation lets blood rush in fast; a ring of tissue then restricts outflow, which is what keeps it firm.

Every link in that chain can be affected by something ordinary: poor sleep and inactivity affect the blood vessels themselves, stress and anxiety interfere with the nervous system signal, and low pelvic floor muscle tone affects how well blood is held in place once it arrives.

That's the whole premise of this program: three separate levers — vascular, muscular, and mental — that each move the same outcome, and each respond to consistent, boring, structured practice.
